# Responsive Design

1. Start from the task and content constraints, not device stereotypes.
2. Define where layouts stop working and create breakpoints accordingly.
3. Keep Clip Studio preview/timeline primary; collapse inspectors into panels/tabs when space is limited.
4. Allow horizontal overflow only inside purposeful areas such as a timeline or data table.
5. Provide touch-sized controls and safe-area support.
6. On mobile, prioritize review, approve/reject, caption corrections, metadata and scheduling; do not pretend a dense multi-track editor works well unless validated.
7. Test 1440, 1280, 1024, 768, 390 and 360 CSS pixel widths (or approved alternatives).
8. Check zoom/reflow, sticky headers, dialogs and overflow.
9. Document feature differences across breakpoints honestly.
